subject: SKU ladder consolidation — channel margin allocation & invoice evidence
messages:
From: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@nexabyte.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: SKU ladder consolidation inquiry

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we scope the private offer for NexaByte, procurement asked me to consolidate the SKU ladder so we can evaluate regional list prices (US/EU) and understand how partner margin will be reflected on our invoices. A few concrete asks from our side:

- Can you provide a single SKU ladder (node-hour tiers + metered addons) that covers both Azure and GCP SKUs so we can compare pricing side-by-side?
- We need a clear mapping of the channel margin: do partners receive a post-invoice pass-through or is it embedded as a rev-share line on Redwood invoices?
- If pass-through, what evidence will you provide (invoice routing sample, distributor PO flow)?

We'd like to close pricing and invoice pathing before legal starts redlines on the SOW. Can you also confirm whether you can issue region-specific invoices (US vs EU) for tax reasons?

Appreciate it — can we get an initial reply by Wednesday?

Best,
Oliver
Head of Procurement
NexaByte Inc.

P.S. attaching our standard SOW template in case you want to pre-populate any billing sections.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@nexabyte.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU ladder consolidation inquiry

Oliver —

Thanks, this is actionable. Quick answers upfront:

- We can produce a consolidated SKU ladder that maps our Azure and GCP SKU families into a single tiered table (node-hour equivalent + metered addon parity).
- Channel margin can be handled either as pass-through (partner invoice line) or as an embedded reseller credit; we recommend pass-through for NexaByte (clean GAAP separation).
- We can provide sample invoice routing evidence (ops artifact) and a partner commission workback. Regional invoices (US/EU) are supported — we'll include tax metadata on each invoice.

Ben/Irine — I looped you because Ben should confirm the margin workback and Irene will own invoice routing/procurement evidence. Oliver, to move fast please share the SOW you mentioned and any required PO/account numbers.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will send the SKU ladder + preliminary margin workback by EOD tomorrow.
2) Ben will share a short workback spreadsheet with both pass-through and embedded-credit scenarios.
3) Irene to attach the invoice evidence checklist (what procurement needs to accept pass-through).

If that works, I'll book a 30-min call Wednesday morning to walk the NexaByte finance team through the two options.

-rachel

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@nexabyte.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SKU ladder consolidation inquiry — initial margin workback

Oliver / Rachel —

Attached is a short workback (channel_margin_workback.xlsx) with two modeled approaches:

1) Pass-through: Redwood invoices NexaByte the gross list price; we then route a separate contract/invoice to the partner (distributor) showing their margin. Pros: clean accounting and partner visibility. Cons: additional invoice reconciliation for NexaByte.

2) Embedded credit (rev-share): Redwood applies a line-item credit on the invoice equal to the partner margin. Pros: simpler for NexaByte accounting. Cons: partner receives credit reconciliation rather than a separate invoice; requires tighter legal mapping.

Key numbers (example tier):
- Tier A (0-10k node-hours): list $0.025/node-hour, partner margin 15% => $0.00375/node-hour
- Tier B (10k-50k): list $0.021/node-hour, partner margin 12%
- Metered add-ons (LLM tokens): list per 1M tokens $8, partner margin 10%

Ben notes: If NexaByte prefers pass-through, we'll need distributor PO number and remit instructions to validate invoice routing in our system. I included a sample routing flow in the sheet.

Let me know any numbers you want me to adjust and I'll regenerate the sheet.

-ben
Ben Carter
Channel Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Rachel/Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from NexaByte finance:

- We prefer pass-through for auditability, but we need the following evidence items before we can accept that flow:
  * Sample Redwood invoice that shows both list items and a separate distributor pass-through line (no PII)
  * A partner commission schedule or partner agreement reference showing the margin percentage for the relevant channel partner
  * Confirmation that Redwood can route invoice copies to our accounting AP mailbox automatically (ap@nexabyte.com)

- On the leadership side, we'd like the ability to see both "gross list" and "net after partner" totals per invoice to reconcile with our procurement system.

We attached the NexaByte SOW (Nexabyte_SOW_v2.pdf) with redlines on the billing section — mostly around invoice delivery cadence and a preferenced billing contact.

Opening to a 30-min call Wednesday 9/23 10:00am PT to finalize. If pass-through is fine, we'll collect the distributor PO and remit details and push legal forward.

Regards,
NexaByte Procurement Team
